title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
description: Find the length of the longest substring with all distinct characters using a shrinkable sliding window.

data.text: Given a string `s`, find the length of the **longest substring** that contains no repeated characters.

**Input:** `s = "abcabcbb"`

**Output:** `3`

**Explanation:** The answer is `"abc"`, with length 3. Note that `"abc"` restarts later, but a substring must be contiguous.
Enumerate all substrings and test each for duplicates with a set. O(n³) if the duplicate check is retried each time — too slow for n = 50,000.

data.title: Brute Force O(n³)
data.content: For each start and end, rebuild a set of characters.

data.text: Keep a window `[left, right]` that contains no duplicates. Expand `right` one character at a time. When a duplicate appears, advance `left` until the window is valid again. Each index enters and leaves the window at most once, so the total work is O(n).

data.title: Sliding Window with a Set O(n)
data.content: Shrink from the left until the incoming character is no longer a duplicate.

data.title: Why the window never needs to shrink past a valid start
data.text: Once we have found a window of length `best`, any shorter window cannot improve the answer. `left` only ever moves forward, which is what keeps the algorithm linear instead of quadratic.
Approach 3: Store the Last Seen Index
Instead of a set, store each character's most recent index. When a duplicate is found, jump `left` directly past the previous occurrence rather than stepping one character at a time.

data.title: Jump-to-index O(n)
data.content: One array lookup replaces the inner shrink loop.

data.title: The off-by-one that breaks this solution
data.text: You must check `lastSeen[c] >= left`. Without the `>= left` guard, a character seen *before* the current window would incorrectly drag `left` backwards, shrinking the window and producing a wrong answer.

data.caption: The window expands on the right until a repeat appears, then the left edge jumps past the previous occurrence.

data.title: Complete solution
data.content: The essential insight: a substring is valid exactly when every character in it is unique, and once a window is invalid you never need to re-examine characters you skipped over.
